Typed Errors (design principle 6)

Status as of v4.9.19: argument validation is wired up; the C++ layer mostly is not.

Two independent mechanisms produce classed conditions.

R-level validators (live, always on). R/validators.R raises pladdrr_input_error conditions directly — you do not need with_pladdrr_errors() to catch them:

tryCatch(
  sound$to_pitch(0, 600, 75),                    # ceiling < floor
  pladdrr_input_error = function(e) e$param      # -> "pitch_ceiling"
)

Conditions carry $routine and $param so callers can branch programmatically. Validators currently covering: pitch range, positive counts/numbers, time_step (0 = auto, matching Praat), quefrency ranges, trend-fit method, positive finite sizes and the 2^29-cell allocation bound (.check_positive_finite(), .check_cell_count()), cochleagram step sizes, and the unit of the Ltas locators ("dB" only).

Data loss (live). When a routine returns something Praat fabricated, pladdrr returns Praat’s value and says so:

w <- tryCatch(sound$extract_part(5, 10), warning = function(w) w)
class(w)   # "pladdrr_data_loss" "pladdrr_warning" "warning" "condition"

Praat zero-pads a window that runs past the signal; goal 1 says reproduce the value, goal 6 says report the fabrication. Controlled by options(pladdrr.data_loss = "warn" | "error" | "silent"); default "warn".

A file can raise it too: src/sound_wrappers.cpp reports a WAV whose data chunk does not match the bytes that follow it — more, and the load returns exactly the samples that exist; fewer, and the load keeps Praat’s shorter count (Praat 6.4.27 answers nx = 4410 for a file holding 1750 samples) while naming the discarded ones. Reached by any file load (Sound(path = ), Sound$new(), deprecated read_sound()); locked in tests/testthat/test-truncated-wav.R.

C++ tags (partially wired). Wrappers can emit tagged messages that with_pladdrr_errors(expr) reclassifies:

PLADDRR_REQUIRE_PTR("routine_name", xptr, "xptr_param_name");
PLADDRR_REQUIRE_FINITE("routine_name", "param_name", value);
PLADDRR_STOP_INPUT("routine_name", "param", "human-readable reason");
PLADDRR_STOP_PRAAT("routine_name", "Praat raised an error doing X");
PLADDRR_WARN_DATA_LOSS("routine_name", "n of m values undefined");

src/batch_queries.cpp and src/sound_wrappers.cpp use them today (the latter PLADDRR_WARN_DATA_LOSS, for a WAV shorter than its own data chunk; the R side muffles it and re-raises it through .warn_data_loss(), which is what applies options(pladdrr.data_loss = )), and src/praat_xptr_utils.h uses PLADDRR_STOP_INPUT for the class check behind the .xptr constructor door and the two file readers. Every other C++ wrapper still raises an untagged error — measured, a bare Rcpp::stop() arrives as Rcpp::exception (e.g. the channel guards’ Channel out of range [0, 3]: 9), and with_pladdrr_errors() cannot class it either because it only reclassifies conditions that carry the tag. So do not assume a pladdrr_praat_error or a pladdrr_input_error will arrive from an arbitrary routine — check before you rely on it.

Class Meaning Where it comes from
pladdrr_input_error invalid argument / precondition fail R validators + C++ require_praat_class()
pladdrr_praat_error Praat internal failure C++ macros (2 sites only)
pladdrr_data_loss output incomplete vs request, or input shorter than its own header R + C++ (live)
pladdrr_decoder_fallback native reader refused the file (MP3/OGG, not FLAC since 5.2.0); av decoded it R (av fallback in .sound_ptr_from_path)

The error classes inherit from pladdrr_error → error → condition, so one tryCatch(pladdrr_error = ...) catches them all; pladdrr_data_loss as a warning and pladdrr_decoder_fallback inherit from pladdrr_warning → warning → condition instead, so catch those as warnings. Both R-level classes are already classed and need no with_pladdrr_errors():

tryCatch(Sound(path = "truncated.wav"),
  pladdrr_data_loss = function(w) conditionMessage(w))       # read N of M samples
suppressWarnings(Sound(path = "song.mp3"))                   # hides pladdrr_decoder_fallback
options(pladdrr.data_loss = "error")                         # does NOT affect decoder_fallback

When porting a new wrapper: call the shared validators at R level, replace bare stop("...") in C++ with the macros above, and emit WARN_DATA_LOSS whenever the result contains NA from out-of-range or undefined input. Lock the behaviour in tests/testthat/test-error-reporting.R.

Performance Audit

Before you time anything, check simd_info()$debug_build. If it is TRUE the shared object was compiled without NDEBUG at -O0 — almost always because devtools::load_all() / pkgbuild::compile_dll() wrote the .o files and a later R CMD INSTALL only relinked them. Every measurement from such a build is 2–7x too slow and worthless. Fix with R CMD INSTALL --preclean .. See the v4.9.22 entry under “What’s New” for the full diagnosis.

Static SIMD + threading inventory: tools/perf_inventory.sh walks src/ and the vendored Praat tree and emits vignettes/agents/performance-inventory.Rmd. Use it to find wrappers that lack an accompanying *_simd.cpp (Phase F SIMD candidates) and to enumerate every MelderThread_PARALLELIZE call site.

Runtime benchmark: inst/benchmarks/run_audit_benchmarks.R times each faithfulness-registry routine against Praat-native execution and writes inst/benchmarks/RESULTS.md with a speedup_vs_praat column. Praat startup is intentionally part of the timing — that cost is real for the “shell out to Praat” alternative the package replaces. Requires R CMD INSTALL . first.

Faithfulness Audit

Design principle 1 — faithfulness to Praat’s own DSP output — is enforced by tests/testthat/test-praat-faithfulness.R, which invokes /Applications/Praat.app/Contents/MacOS/Praat --run against an extensible registry of routines in tests/testthat/faithfulness/routines.R, compares the output to the matching pladdrr call at a per-routine tolerance, and emits vignettes/agents/faithfulness-report.Rmd (set PLADDRR_FAITHFULNESS_OUTDIR to regenerate it; the caveats in it live in the test file, and the report names the Praat version it ran against). Always name the Praat version with a reference number: the vendored source tracks 6.4.47, and the CPPS pipeline differs from 6.4.27 by about 0.13 dB (Praat rewrote its CPP-to-CPPS post-processing); against 6.4.47 all 19 registry rows pass and CPPS is 0.003 dB away. tests/testthat/test-fidelity-fingerprint.R is the second gate: 89 numbers from one signal, no oracle needed, refuses any ERR/NA row.

When porting a new Praat routine into pladdrr, add a registry row. Default tolerance is 0 for exact-arithmetic routines; looser tolerances require a written rationale in the row. Failing rows are first-class regressions.

Quick Start for Agents

This guide provides the complete API reference for pladdrr, an R package that provides direct access to Praat C++ functionality. When reimplementing Praat code in R:

  1. Object Creation: Use function constructors (not R6 classes): Sound(), Pitch(), etc.
  2. Method Calls: Use $ syntax: sound$to_pitch(), pitch$get_mean()
  3. Units: Specify as strings: "hertz", "bark", "db" (converted internally to codes)
  4. Class Names: Use clean names for inherits() checks: Formant, Pitch, Intensity (not internal *_constructor names) (a Praat Matrix is a PraatMatrix, class vector c("PraatMatrix", "PraatObject"); see PraatMatrix and the ‘Matrix’ package)
  5. Batch Operations: Use batch query functions when extracting multiple values
  6. Vectorized Methods: Use $get_*_windows(), $get_*_vector(), $get_spectral_moments_batch() for 14-150x speedups (Patterns 2i, 2p)
  7. Properties: Fast access via .cpp$property or backward-compatible get_property() methods
  8. Pipeline Operations: Use two_pass_adaptive_pitch() and get_jitter_shimmer_batch() for voice quality (Pattern 2k)
  9. Tier 4 Ultra API: Use get_durations_batch(), calculate_f0_stats_ultra(), calculate_minimum_intensity_ultra(), get_voice_quality_ultra() for DSI workflows, plus calculate_cpps_ultra(), extract_voiced_segments_ultra(), calculate_multiband_hnr_ultra() for simple AVQI/VQ workflows. For repeated intervals on the same sound, build once with build_multiband_harmonicity() and query with multiband_hnr_stats() (Pattern 2l)
  10. Fidelity target: Every re-implemented Praat procedure must achieve r > 0.95 vs Praat on ≥50 real files before shipping. Use the in-repo Praat faithfulness registry and audit benchmark runner (see Re-implementing a Praat Procedure).
  11. Praat Matrix objects: construct with PraatMatrix() and test with inherits(m, "PraatMatrix"); read the numbers with as.matrix(m) or m$as_matrix(). Matrix() and inherits(m, "Matrix") no longer exist/hold. See PraatMatrix and the ‘Matrix’ package.

Tier 4 Ultra: Hardcoded Algorithm Choices

Every Tier 4 “Ultra” function that touches pitch/harmonicity picks one Praat algorithm internally (raw AC vs. raw CC, veryAccurate true/false, fixed threshold constants) so the whole pipeline can run in one C++ call. Some of that choice is exposed as an R parameter, some is hardcoded to match a specific reference Praat script. Check this table before assuming an Ultra function is configurable, or before porting a Praat script that expects a different algorithm — the alternative is discovering the mismatch via a Praat-vs-R diff test (see get_voice_quality_ultra()’s AC-vs-CC history) or reading the C++ source directly.

Function Pitch/harmonicity algorithm Configurable Matches
calculate_f0_stats_ultra() Sound_to_Pitch_rawCc, veryAccurate = TRUE, silenceThreshold = 0.03 voicing_threshold only DSI201.praat To Pitch (cc)...
calculate_minimum_intensity_ultra() Sound_to_Pitch_rawCc, veryAccurate = FALSE, silenceThreshold = 0.03, voicingThreshold = 0.8 (hardcoded, not exposed) none DSI201.praat IM component (stricter voicing threshold than the jitter block)
get_voice_quality_ultra() Sound_to_Pitch_rawCc or rawAc via pitch_method ("cc"/"ac"), very_accurate pitch_method, very_accurate DSI201.praat (default "cc"); pitch_method = "periodic_cc" is an alias for "ac" + very_accurate = FALSE, which is byte-for-byte Praat’s Sound: To PointProcess (periodic, cc)... (see Sound_to_PointProcess.cpp: that command is defined as Sound_to_Pitch() + Sound_Pitch_to_PointProcess_cc, and Sound_to_Pitch() is Sound_to_Pitch_rawAc(..., veryAccurate=false, 0.03,0.45,0.01,0.35,0.14))
calculate_multiband_hnr_ultra() Sound_to_Harmonicity_cc (no AC option) none VQ_measurements_V2.praat lines 102-122
calculate_cpps_ultra() n/a — pitch-independent, built on Sound_to_PowerCepstrogram see CPPS parameter table in /CLAUDE.md —
extract_voiced_segments_ultra() n/a — voiced/silence split is Intensity-threshold based, not pitch-based silence_threshold_db, min_pitch (controls the Intensity window, not a pitch algorithm choice) —

Each function’s own ?function_name help has a matching @section Algorithm choice: block with the same fact, so this table and the roxygen never need to be read in isolation.

Data Flow Example: sound$to_pitch_cc()

Shared Dispatch Table Architecture (v4.8.33, optimized v4.9.18)

  1. User calls: pitch <- sound$to_pitch_cc(pitch_floor = 75, pitch_ceiling = 600)
  2. $.Sound S3 dispatch looks up to_pitch_cc in .sound_methods env
  3. Instance methods call the Rcpp module object, .self$.cpp$method(), which is the single implementation of that getter (Formant, Spectrogram, Spectrum, Sound, Table queries, PowerCepstrum get_peak_prominence, DurationTier save were consolidated here; earlier releases had a parallel .Call wrapper copy that was removed). Transforms that build a new object and batch/threaded routines still call Rcpp::export functions (.sound_to_pitch_ac(.self$.xptr, ...), batch_queries.cpp), because no module method exists for them.
  4. C++ calls Praat function (Sound_to_Pitch_cc(), Formant_getValueAtTime(), etc.)
  5. Result wrapped in XPtr<structPitch> with custom deleter
  6. R wrapper creates new Pitch() from pointer via factory function
  7. Returns: structure(list(.xptr = ptr, .cpp = module), class = c("Pitch", "PraatObject"))

Key Performance Improvements: - Shared dispatch tables eliminate per-instance closure allocation (9x faster creation, 160x less memory, v4.8.32). - Instance queries go through the Rcpp module (.self$.cpp$x()); the v4.9.18 direct-.Call wrapper path for these was removed in 2026-11 to eliminate duplicate implementations (see pitfall 16).

Object Structure (Shared Dispatch Table Pattern)

All 36 wrappers use the Shared Dispatch Table pattern (v4.8.33, extended since):

All wrappers use a shared .{type}_methods environment + $.Type S3 dispatch. PraatInterpreter is the only R6Class — it requires persistent mutable state and reference semantics.

# Shared method table (one per type, not per instance)
.pitch_methods <- new.env(hash = TRUE, parent = emptyenv())
.pitch_methods$get_mean <- function(.self, ...) .self$.cpp$get_mean(...)
.pitch_methods$to_point_process <- function(.self, ...) { ... }
# ... all methods take .self as first arg
lockEnvironment(.pitch_methods, bindings = TRUE)

# Constructor: minimal list, no closures
Pitch <- function(.xptr = NULL) {
  pitch_mod <- get_module("pitch_module")
  cpp_obj <- pitch_mod$RPitch$new(.xptr)
  structure(list(.xptr = .xptr, .cpp = cpp_obj), class = c("Pitch", "PraatObject"))
}

# S3 dispatch: $.Pitch intercepts field/method access
`$.Pitch` <- function(x, name) {
  val <- .subset2(x, name)       # Fast path: .xptr, .cpp
  if (!is.null(val)) return(val)
  method <- .pitch_methods[[name]]
  if (is.null(method)) return(NULL)
  function(...) method(x, ...)    # Bind self, return closure
}

.xptr is a checked door, not a bare cast (5.1.0): RType$new(ptr) is where Rcpp reinterprets the external pointer as the wrapper’s C++ struct, so that module constructor is the last place a wrong-class pointer can still be refused. Every module constructor that takes one (src/modules/*_module.cpp, 37 types plus Matrix and PitchTier) calls require_praat_class() (src/praat_xptr_utils.h, Praat’s Thing_isa subclass test — so an Ltas or Sound pointer still passes as a Matrix), and the R constructor wraps the call in with_pladdrr_errors(), so the refusal is a classed pladdrr_input_error naming the class found (“Not a Sound (found TextGrid)”). PowerCepstrogram has no module object of its own; its constructor builds one only to run the check. Without the check the first field read after construction is out of bounds and the R session dies uncatchably. A new wrapper type needs both halves; the list of types is in tests/testthat/test-xptr-all-constructors.R.

Special cases: Some wrappers have additional fields or no .xptr: - FormantPath, KlattGrid, ComplexSpectrogram: no .xptr — only .cpp stored - PowerCepstrogram: opposite of the above — pure .xptr, no .cpp module at all - Electroglottogram: triple class c("Electroglottogram", "Sound", "PraatObject") + .pointer compat alias - AmplitudeTier: .pointer compat alias in $ dispatch (used by factory functions) - PitchTier, FormantTier, LongSound, VocalTract: static $.{type}_constructor for class methods

Intentionally R6 (1/37): PraatInterpreter (requires persistent mutable state for script execution)

Object Types

Note: ~41 distinct object types are wrapped in R, backed by 39 src/modules/*.cpp files (not a 1:1 mapping — some types like MelSpectrogram/BarkSpectrogram/LFCC/PowerCepstrogram share or lack a dedicated module file, while some modules like Electroglottogram/DTW/Polygon aren’t broken out as separate rows below).

Update v4.8.25: Added MelSpectrogram and BarkSpectrogram modules for psychoacoustic analysis. Update v4.0.7: Added MFCC, LFCC, FormantModeler, PCA, Discriminant modules for speaker recognition, robust formant tracking, and statistical analysis.

Interpreter (NEW in v2.1.0)

Type Creation Method Purpose
PraatInterpreter PraatInterpreter$new() Persistent Praat script interpreter with variable state

NOTE: PraatInterpreter is the only object that uses R6::R6Class. All other ~40 object types use the shared dispatch table pattern (v4.8.33). This is intentional — the interpreter requires persistent mutable state, reference semantics, and method chaining (self reference).

Key Methods: - run(script) - Execute Praat script - eval(expr) - Evaluate expression (tries numeric, then string, then vector, then string array) - get_variable(name) - Get interpreter variable - set_variable(name, value) - Set interpreter variable

Example:

interp <- PraatInterpreter$new()
interp$run('x = 42')
interp$run('y = x * 2')
result <- interp$eval('y')  # 84 (numeric tried first, then string)

Unit Code Reference

Frequency Units (Pitch, Formant)

Every pitch door (Pitch$ methods, PitchTier$, the batch queries, praat-direct.R) now resolves the string through one table, .pitch_unit_code() in R/utils-internal.R, which is Praat’s kPitch_unit enum (src/praat.github.io/fon/Pitch_enums.h). An unknown string raises pladdrr_input_error; it no longer falls back to hertz. Use the strings; the codes are listed only for reading C++.

Code kPitch_unit R string(s)
0 HERTZ "hertz", "hz"
1 HERTZ_LOGARITHMIC "hertz_logarithmic"
2 MEL "mel"
3 LOG_HERTZ "loghertz"
4 SEMITONES_1 "semitones_re_1hz"
5 SEMITONES_100 "semitones_re_100hz", "semitones", "st"
6 SEMITONES_200 "semitones_re_200hz"
7 SEMITONES_440 "semitones_re_440hz"
8 ERB "erb"

A bare "semitones" is Praat’s default, semitones re 100 Hz. Before 5.1.1 four tables disagreed with the enum: unit = "semitones" and "erb" returned log10(Hz) from Pitch$ methods, and the direct getters answered "loghertz" in semitones re 1 Hz.

Formant Units

R String Code Praat Enum
"hertz" 0 kFormant_unit::HERTZ
"bark" 1 kFormant_unit::BARK

Intensity Units

There is no general-purpose “intensity unit” code. The only related parameter is averaging_method on Intensity$get_mean(from_time, to_time, averaging_method), internally mapped by .intensity_avg_code (R/intensity-wrapper.R) onto Praat’s Intensity_averaging enum (fon/Intensity.h:64-67); the returned number is always in dB, and any other string is an error:

R String Code What it averages
"median" 0 0.5 quantile of the contour
"energy" 1 mean of 10^(dB/10), re-expressed in dB (DEFAULT)
"sones" 2 mean of 2^(dB/10), re-expressed in dB
"db" 3 arithmetic mean of the dB values

This is not the LTAS averaging enum (which has no median; see “LTAS Units” below). The integer APIs intensity_get_mean_direct() and intensity_get_statistics_batch() take the same raw codes and default to 0 = median; Praat’s legacy two-argument Intensity: Get mean: from, to is the plain dB mean (= 3), so those defaults are a pladdrr convention, not an oracle match. Intensity$get_statistics(… , metrics = "mean") and print()’s “Mean intensity” line use energy (= 1), the same number get_mean() returns by default.

LTAS Units (fixed again in v5.1.0 — the v4.0.4 table this section used to carry was wrong)

Five Ltas queries take a unit argument — get_mean(fmin, fmax, unit), get_means_batch(fmins, fmaxs, unit), get_standard_deviation(fmin, fmax, unit), get_slope(f1min, f1max, f2min, f2max, unit) and get_local_peak_height(environment_min, environment_max, peak_min, peak_max, unit) — and the number they return is always in dB, whatever unit you name. unit selects the domain the average is taken in; Praat’s own queries convert the result back (Sampled_getMean_standardUnit, fon/Sampled.cpp:505-509, and Sampled_getStandardDeviation_standardUnit, fon/Sampled.cpp:550-554, called at fon/praat_uvafon_init.cpp:1107 and :1156). .ltas_unit_code (R/ltas-wrapper.R) maps the string onto Praat’s Ltas averaging CHOICE, which is 1-based and has no median (fon/praat_uvafon_init.cpp:1101-1105); any other string is an error:

R String Code What it averages Returned
"energy" 1 mean of 10^(dB/10) that mean converted back: 10*log10(...) dB
"sones" 2 mean of 2^(dB/10) that mean converted back: 10*log2(...) dB
"dB" 3 arithmetic mean of the dB values (DEFAULT) the dB mean itself

get_slope() and get_local_peak_height() compare two band averages: code 3 subtracts them, the other two divide them and convert the ratio back (fon/Ltas.cpp:83-97). Code 3 — not 0 — is what selects the dB branch, which is why "dB" must map to 3.

Three other Ltas queries — get_value_at_frequency(), get_minimum(), get_maximum() — also accept a unit argument, but they read bins that are already in dB and Praat’s dialogs for them have no unit. They accept only "dB" (any case) and raise a pladdrr_input_error for anything else (before 5.1.0 the argument was silently ignored).

A band average covers the whole bins between the two frequencies, weighting the bins at an incomplete range edge by the fraction of the bin inside the range; pladdrr does not interpolate between bins here, because Praat’s Ltas queries pass interpolate = false (fon/praat_uvafon_init.cpp:1108, :1159). Values are frozen against the oracle in tests/testthat/test-ltas-averaging-unit.R.

Wrong in earlier editions of this guide: the table read "db" | 0 | Passthrough, and the 10*log10(ratio) → dB column described the conversion helper rather than the unit of the answer. Both readings cost users numbers: unit = "energy" returned the linear mean (14170.064098 where Praat prints 41.513718 dB), and get_slope() with its default unit = "dB" returned a dimensionless ratio (-0.115522) instead of -31.906946 dB.

# All three answers are dB; they differ because the average is taken in three domains:
ltas$get_mean(0, 0, unit = "dB")       # -22.832719   mean of the bins
ltas$get_mean(0, 0, unit = "energy")   #  41.513718   mean of 10^(dB/10), back in dB
ltas$get_mean(0, 0, unit = "sones")    #  -1.519995   mean of 2^(dB/10), back in dB

# Spectral tilt in dB — the default spelling now works (values: inst/extdata/test.flac):
ltas$get_slope(0, 1000, 1000, 4000, unit = "dB")        # -31.906946
ltas$get_slope(0, 1000, 1000, 4000, unit = "energy")    # -52.513078

Interpolation Methods

Updated v2.1.1: Fixed intensity interpolation codes.

Code Method Use Case
0 Nearest Fast, no smoothing
1 Linear Moderate smoothing
2 Cubic Smooth curves (DEFAULT for intensity)
3 Sinc70 High-quality, 70-point window
4 Sinc700 Highest quality, 700-point window

String API (recommended):

# Use string names - automatically converted to codes
intensity$get_value_at_time(time = 1.0, interpolation = "cubic")
get_intensity_at_times(intensity, times, interpolate = "sinc70")
